claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for the planned controlled rollout is policy-compliant and evidentially supported because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the known tax filing assistant weakness can be handled through controlled launch plus explicit disclosure and monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use `compliant` only if admissible evidence shows certification includes the required disclosure or approved risk acceptance covering the exposed segment.
Use `noncompliant` if certification is presented as unqualified despite the exposed weakness and absent disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Use `suspicious` if the packet plausibly supports a limited certification theory but overclaims or leaves the required disclosure predicate unresolved.
Public guidance on model cards and AI risk management can support monitoring and documentation practices, but cannot override the stated internal policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide the exact model-card or launch disclosure text that will accompany certification and cover the tax filing assistant limitation.
Provide approved risk acceptance if the organization intends to rely on that exception instead of disclosure.
Provide the certification artifact or decision memo showing certification is explicitly conditioned on disclosure for the exposed segment.
Provide evidence of materiality assessment for the tax filing assistant weakness if the actor contends the limitation is not material.
specific_concerns: The affected tax filing assistant segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has no approver, and does not address the exposed tax filing assistant segment.
Policy text says rollout controls and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.

unsupported_claims: Any unqualified certification decision is unsupported unless it is expressly conditioned on disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
